workshopGuides.title: Programming LEDs
workshopGuides.hook: Flash an ESP32-C3, light up an LED strip, then change the code and make it do something new.

topics.title: How one wire drives a whole strip of LEDs
topics.hook: No LED on the strip has an address. So how does LED 7 know which color is its?
topics.post: No LED on an addressable strip has an address. Watch how one wire tells a whole strip what to do, and the ways it fails silently.

topics.title: Why delay() makes your project ignore you
topics.hook: Press the button. The board with delay() will miss most of your presses.
topics.post: Press the button. The board using delay() misses most presses. The one using millis() never does. A 3-minute interactive explainer.

topics.title: Baud rate: why your serial monitor shows garbage
topics.hook: "­¾ýÿ¿þ" in your serial monitor is good news: the wiring works, only the speed is wrong.
topics.description: Garbage characters in your serial monitor are good news: the wiring works, only the speed is wrong.
topics.post: Garbage characters in your serial monitor? Your wiring is probably fine. See exactly why a baud-rate mismatch scrambles text, with a live decoder.

topics.title: The USB cable that looks fine and isn’t
topics.hook: The board lights up, but your laptop can’t see it. It’s probably the cable.
topics.post: Board lights up but your computer can’t see it? Charge-only USB cables look identical to data cables. See what’s missing inside.

topics.title: How many LEDs can USB power?
topics.hook: A ten-LED strip on full white can draw more than a USB port supplies, and the board starts rebooting.
topics.post: Why does my LED strip keep rebooting the board on white? An interactive look at how much current LEDs draw, and how much USB can give.

topics.title: ESP32-C3 SuperMini pinout, explained
topics.hook: Sixteen pins, a few with surprises. Tap any pin to see what it does.
topics.post: An interactive pinout for the tiny ESP32-C3 SuperMini: tap any pin to see what it does, including the three that can stop your board from booting.

topics.title: Multimeter probes: which jack is which
topics.hook: Black goes in COM. Red goes in V almost every time. The jacks marked A are the ones that blow fuses.
topics.post: Black probe, red probe, three or four jacks with tiny labels. Click to plug them in and find out which jack is which, and which one blows fuses.

topics.title: Continuity: is this wire actually connected?
topics.hook: Touch the probes to both ends of a wire. A beep means it’s connected. Silence means it isn’t.
topics.post: Is this wire actually connected? The multimeter’s beep setting answers in a second. Try it on a good wire, a broken one and a switch.

topics.title: Measuring voltage with a multimeter
topics.hook: Check a battery, then the 5V and 3.3 pins on your board. And find out what the minus sign means.
topics.post: Measure a battery and your ESP32 board’s 5V and 3.3V pins with a multimeter, and learn what a minus sign or a lone 1 on the display means.

topics.title: Measuring current without blowing the fuse
topics.hook: To measure current the meter goes in the circuit, not across it. Put it across a battery and the fuse blows.
topics.post: Measuring current is the one multimeter job that blows fuses. See why the meter goes in the circuit, not across it, and measure an LED’s 18 mA.

topics.title: Which solder wire should you buy?
topics.hook: Leaded or lead-free, thick or thin, and the one kind that must never touch a circuit board.
topics.post: Leaded or lead-free? 0.8 mm or 1.6 mm? And why plumbing solder ruins circuit boards. A quick, interactive guide to picking solder wire for electronics.

topics.title: What temperature should your soldering iron be?
topics.hook: Too cold makes a dull, weak joint. Too hot burns the flux and lifts the pad. Find the window.
topics.post: Too cold gives a dull, grainy joint. Too hot burns the flux and lifts pads. Turn the dial and find the window for leaded and lead-free solder, and see why tip size matters.

topics.title: Tin first, then join
topics.hook: Two surfaces already coated in solder flow together in a second. Bare ones fight you.
topics.post: The trick that makes soldering wires easy: tin the wire, tin the pad, then join them. Try it both ways and compare.

topics.title: Spot the bad solder joint
topics.hook: A good joint looks like a tiny shiny volcano. Can you name what went wrong with the others?
topics.post: Cold, dry, bridged, blobbed or cooked? A quick quiz: spot the bad solder joint, then learn what caused it and how to fix it.

topics.title: Why your soldering tip stopped working
topics.hook: A black tip won’t take solder, however hot it is. Here’s how it got that way, and how to keep it shiny.
topics.post: A black soldering tip won’t take solder, however hot you run it. See what oxidizes a tip, and the two habits that keep it shiny for years.

topics.title: Soldering header pins onto the ESP32-C3 SuperMini
topics.hook: Use a breadboard as a jig, tack two opposite corners, and the pins come out straight every time.
topics.post: Straight header pins on the first try: use a breadboard as a jig and tack two opposite corners first. A step-by-step guide for the ESP32-C3 SuperMini.
